claims.text: Five-or-more-metal alloys in approximately equiatomic ratios can form single-phase solid solutions.
The initial nanoparticles have a homogeneous, approximately equiatomic elemental distribution.
Retention of a single-phase solid solution is governed by competition between thermodynamic phase-separation or ordering tendencies and kinetic barriers.
Configurational entropy can stabilize a multicomponent solid solution, particularly as temperature increases.
Favorable chemical-ordering enthalpy can overcome configurational entropy at low temperature.
Atomic-size mismatch produces significant lattice distortion in the relevant nanoparticles.
Lattice distortion enhances the thermodynamic stability of a single-phase solid solution relative to phase separation or ordering.
Lattice distortion raises the effective activation energy for atomic diffusion.
High diffusion barriers and sluggish kinetics can suppress elemental segregation and preserve a uniform elemental distribution during annealing.
Inert or reducing atmospheres preserve the proposed high diffusion barriers.
Oxidizing environments chemically modify surface atoms and reduce diffusion barriers.
Reduced diffusion barriers in oxidizing environments facilitate local chemical reordering or demixing.
Under inert or reducing conditions, the nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous single-phase structure with minimal segregation throughout 473–1923 K.
Under oxidizing conditions, high temperature will cause greater surface segregation or emergent secondary phases than under inert or reducing conditions.
The as-synthesized baseline has minimal lattice strain at ambient temperature.
The proposed mechanism should apply only when lattice distortion is significant and diffusion is sluggish.
External supports or atypical gas pressures may alter diffusion kinetics and invalidate the prediction.
The cited nanoparticle simulations show uniform elemental distributions after annealing at 773 K, while full diffusion equilibration produces segregation.

contradictions.description: The baseline specifies minimal lattice strain, whereas the proposed mediator, mechanism, and applicability boundary require significant lattice distortion to stabilize the particles. The hypothesis does not explain when or how the required distortion develops from the minimally strained baseline.
